mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks, moving from -8.3% to -3.4%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal or stagnation of the recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, from 6.9% to 5.7%, indicates fewer people staying home and a shift towards out-of-home activities. If RESIDENTIAL drops below 5.5% in the next week, it will trigger an increase in RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.5% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks, or even decreases.

mechanism_narrative: The combined slight recovery in TRANSIT mobility (from -6.7% to -3.1%) and stable WORKPLACES mobility (around -3.9%) indicates a cautious return to daily routines. If both TRANSIT continues its upward trend and WORKPLACES remains stable or increases, it will drive RETAIL_REC higher as more people commute and engage in post-work activities.
failure_condition: Despite TRANSIT continuing its upward trend and WORKPLACES remaining stable or increasing, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of stable mobility, the recent volatility in PARKS mobility (e.g., -22.0% to -25.0% then to -21.0%) suggests that people are seeking outdoor recreation. If this trend continues, it will divert some discretionary spending from indoor retail, causing RETAIL_REC to decrease over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS volatility continues (e.g., week-on-week change > 2 points)
failure_condition: PARKS volatility continues but RETAIL_REC increases or remains stable over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT) and the downward trend in RESIDENTIAL strongly imply an ongoing easing of public health restrictions. This policy shift will continue to boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as more activities become permissible.
failure_condition: Despite the observed trends, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an increase, suggesting a halt or reversal of policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: The high and stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (around 40%) indicates a consistent baseline level of essential activity. This stability suggests that basic needs are being met, freeing up capacity for discretionary spending and driving a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains stable but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The stagnation of WORKPLACES mobility at a slightly negative level (around -3.9%) suggests that a significant portion of the workforce is not returning to offices, limiting potential weekday retail activity and causing RETAIL_REC to remain stagnant or slightly decrease over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains stagnant, but RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous upward trend in TRANSIT (from -6.7% to -3.1%), PARKS (from -27.1% to -21.0%), and RETAIL_REC (from -8.3% to -3.4%) indicates a broad-based increase in out-of-home activities. This synchronized recovery suggests growing public confidence and will collectively push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite the observed synchronized upward trends, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, indicating a decoupling of these activity patterns.
